en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
Gabbhinīvagga 68.
The Training Rule on Co-residents.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the nun Thullanandā, having given the full admission to a co-resident nun, neither herself assisted her for two years nor had her assisted;
those nuns were foolish and incompetent,
and they did not know what was allowable or what was unallowable.
Those bhikkhunīs who were modest … [as before] … complained, grumbled, and spread it about, saying:
“How can the noble lady Thullanandā, having had her co-resident ordained, neither herself assist her nor cause another to assist her for two years? … [The Buddha asked:
“Is it true, bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having had her co-resident ordained, neither herself assists her nor causes another to assist her for two years?”

“It is true, Blessed One. The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her: “… How can the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having given the full admission to a co-resident, neither herself support her for two years nor cause her to be supported? This is not suitable, bhikkhunīs. … [as before] … “And how, bhikkhunīs, is it in this way: that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having given the full admission to a co-resident, neither herself supports her for two years nor causes her to be supported? … [as before] … “It is not, bhikkhunīs, for the sake of training those who have already been trained that this rule of training is laid down; rather, it is for the sake of training those who have not yet been trained that this rule of training is laid down. … [as before] … “If a bhikkhunī, having given the full admission to a co-resident, does not herself support her for two years nor cause her to be supported, she commits an offense of wrong-doing. … [as before] … “In this case, ‘co-resident’ means one who has received the full admission together with her. … [as before] … “In this case, ‘two years’ means two rains-retreats.

… [as before] … “If a bhikkhunī, having given the full admission to a co-resident, does not herself support her for two years nor cause her to be supported, she commits an offense of wrong-doing. … [as before] … “There is no offense if she is unable to support her; if she is ill; if she is afflicted by pain; if she is insane; if she is the first offender. … [as before] … “And how, bhikkhunīs, is there no offense? Here, bhikkhunīs, a bhikkhunī gives the full admission to a co-resident. She herself supports her for two years and causes her to be supported. There is no offense. … [as before] … “And how, bhikkhunīs, is there no offense? Here, bhikkhunīs, a bhikkhunī gives the full admission to a co-resident. She is unable to support her, but she causes her to be supported. There is no offense. … [as before] … “And how, bhikkhunīs, is there no offense? “Monks, this does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
And thus, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule:
‘If any nun, having given the full admission to a co-resident, neither herself supports her nor causes her to be supported for two years, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).’”
"But whichever" means whichever such... "nun" means...
[as before]... nun.
...pe... this is the "bhikkhunī" intended in this context.
A "sahajīvinī" is called a *saddhivihārinī* (a co-resident).
"Having caused to go forth" means having conferred full ordination.
"Two years" means...
For two years.
"He should not encourage" means he should not himself encourage [them] by means of recitation, interrogation, exhortation, and instruction.
"Should not cause to be looked after" means she should not command another, thinking,
"For two years I will neither look after them myself nor cause another to look after them. At the mere moment of relinquishing her responsibility, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
There is no offense if there is an obstacle, or if,
having sought it out, one does not find it.
For one who is ill,
in times of distress,
or for one who is insane.
"For one who is a first-offender.
The eighth training rule is concluded.
